Apple has updated the Apple Store app's privacy policy to include terms related to an upcoming virtual shopping assistant. Details below.

Apple is expanding its use of artificial intelligence in retail operations

According to MacRumors, the Apple Store app and its privacy page now feature a new section titled "Virtual Shopping Assistant," with the following content:

In other words, the Apple Store app may soon have a built-in chatbot that uses user data to provide personalised responses and help users make purchasing decisions.

Apple states that before sharing chat content with anonymous partners that power the assistant's responses, it will first strip out personally identifiable information — a strong hint that at least part of the experience will be driven by third-party models from external companies.

Chat history will be stored within the app for easy reference, and also retained for Apple's business analysis purposes. Users can opt in or out of allowing their conversations to be used to improve the virtual shopping assistant through a new "Chat Improvements" setting.

The wording in Apple's privacy policy suggests the virtual assistant will initially roll out in select countries and regions, likely debuting in English-speaking markets before expanding to more languages and regions.

Months before this news surfaced, Apple had already added an AI-powered chatbot to its Sales Coach app to provide retail partners with sales and technical resources. Users can access the chatbot via the "Ask" tab, which draws on Apple's official training materials and documentation to answer questions.

Separately, Bloomberg previously reported that Apple has been testing a system called "Live Notes" in select retail stores, using AI to record, transcribe and summarise Genius Bar sessions so staff can focus on customers without having to take notes themselves.
